Fixes (this release):
- A triple-quote (''') multiline string containing ANY non-ASCII character (wide-string path:
  sourcecodepage=CP_UTF8, e.g. {$mode delphiunicode} or {$codepage utf8}) no longer crashes the
  compiler with an internal EAccessViolation. The scanner's postprocessutf8multiline was
  upstream-broken: it used the stale ASCII length (reset to 0 by the utf-8 conversion), indexed
  the 0-based widestring 1-based, appended into the wrong buffer, then dereferenced a nil buffer.
- A badly-INDENTED non-ASCII multiline string now yields the existing meaningful error
  "Incorrectly indented multi-line string (need N whitespace chars) starting at line L, column C"
  instead of an internal compiler error (God mrig72jt).
- Properly-indented non-ASCII multiline strings now compile with codepoint-exact content
  (indentation-stripped per the closing-quote column, as for ASCII strings).
- Backtick (`) multiline strings and ASCII-only ''' strings are unchanged.

Upstream-broken routine (byte-identical to fpc-unleashed/main at fix time; fixed forward in
vibepascal per Policy #40). Carries v50 m_stringordcast explicit-casts-only + v49 compile-time
{$if SizeOf/High(Char)} + v48 String/Char Delphi parity.
Verified on Linux x86_64: isolated A/B (baseline v50 232e773f vs fix) -- 4 ICE variants flip
(2 bad-indent -> clean error, 2 good-indent -> compile+run content-exact); full tests/test/ A/B
(1973 tests) = ZERO regression; new guards tests/test/tmultilinestring38 ({%fail} clean error) +
tmultilinestring39 (run, content-exact); stage2==stage3 byte-identical fixpoint (ba5c0e3f);
vp_win64_smoke PASS exit 0 on the production binary.
Win64 RUNTIME verification pending downstream (cannot exec a Win64 binary on the Linux build host).
